title: Affinity-hash collision in routing table sends Dedicated tenant to legacy quantized variant
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A production bug in the routing-table rebuild logic causes an affinity-hash collision for a subset of batched requests from Dedicated tenants. Colliding entries were incorrectly deduplicated, which left requests mapped to a stale legacy quantized model variant in a different region. Customer-facing symptoms: elevated latency and quality regressions for a high-volume enterprise tenant during Dedicated saturation events. Impact window: 2026-03-09 18:27 UTC to 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC. Root cause (high level): a change to the routing-table compaction routine introduced a non-deterministic bucket erase when two affinity keys hashed to the same bucket; the compact path prioritized older entries but failed to respect tenant-scoped model-version boundaries, effectively promoting a legacy variant to the winning route for N% of colliding keys.
repro_steps: 1) Configure Dedicated pool with tenant affinity and a mix of canonical + quantized variants
2) Send high QPS batched requests with identical prefix lengths to force same affinity hash bucket
3) Trigger routing-table compaction via simulated saturation (scale-down/scale-up cycle)
4) Observe route chosen includes legacy quantized variant for some requests (compare model.variant in request logs)
5) Confirm by replaying traces against staging routing service with identical compaction behavior
customer_escalations: CS-9981 (enterprise tenant reported quality regression and SLA miss)
Support case: #87234 - customer observed repeated model downgrades during peak
mitigation: Immediate: Disabled compaction path that performs in-place bucket dedupe (rolled back 2026-03-10 02:20 UTC)
Workaround: Forced tenant-scoped routing evaluation on the edge (temporary policy applied)
Customer comms: Notified affected tenant at 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC with post-incident acknowledgement and mitigation steps
temporary_fixes_deployed: policy/tenant-scope-enforced - gating rule applied to Dedicated for 4 hours during peak
plan: 1) Add strong tenant and model-version guard to compaction routine so entries from different tenant-scopes cannot collide across variant decisions
2) Replace in-place dedupe with stable-merge algorithm that preserves newest non-stale entry per tenant
3) Add deterministic hashing test coverage and property tests for compaction under saturation
4) Run a staged rollout: canary on staging Dedicated pool -> canary in small subset of prod -> full roll
5) Post-incident retro & update runbook for affinity-collision incidents
test_plan: Unit tests for compaction stable-merge behavior (edge cases: identical hashes, cross-tenant keys)
Simulated chaos test that creates repeated compaction during high QPS batches
Integration test: end-to-end routing with Dedicated pool under scale events to assert no cross-tenant promotions
Perf regression tests to ensure compaction change does not degrade routing throughput
linked_prs: github.com/redwood/repo/pulls/11866 - add deterministic hashing property tests
notes: Decision trade-offs: We initially implemented in-place dedupe to reduce routing-table memory churn. That optimization assumed tenant-key uniqueness which is not guaranteed under cross-tenant hashing; correcting it reintroduces some allocation overhead but avoids incorrect variant promotion.
Operational: After fix we'll add a background validator job that scans routing-table buckets for cross-tenant collisions and alerts if any are found.
Follow-ups: schedule a capacity-focused session with runtime team to evaluate alternative compaction strategies that maintain memory bounds without sacrificing tenant isolation.
